label: Teams get smaller
title: The unit of delivery stops being the team of eight
thesis: The standard delivery unit in software may be shrinking. If a small group with machine support can carry work that previously needed a full team, the consequences run past headcount into how work is coordinated, how careers progress, and what a manager is for. The early reports come from forerunners and investors rather than from the field, so the size of the change is far less clear than its direction.
currentPressure: Organisations are reporting delivery from markedly smaller groups while overall demand for engineers has not fallen, so the pressure shows up in team composition rather than in total employment.

implications.statement: Coordination overhead that justified larger teams shifts towards coordinating machine work instead of coordinating people.
Fewer, broader roles replace narrow specialisms, and the rungs a career climbs through get further apart.
Managing five people plus substantial machine capacity is a different job from managing ten people, and is not yet a defined one.

evidence.note: engineering teams reported shrinking from 8-10 to five or fewer
635+ leaders report the challenge shifting from adoption to accountability
30,000 roles cut to fund infrastructure — restructuring driven by AI spend, not by team-level productivity
AI becomes the leading stated reason for US job cuts, at 25% of the monthly total
engineering roles doubled since the 2023 trough with 67,000+ open positions
engineering among the most resilient functions across 80 million companies tracked

reachRationale: A single investor field writeup reports teams shrinking to five or fewer, and the surrounding layoff data is driven by infrastructure spending rather than by team-level productivity. This is a forerunner observation that has not been replicated across independent contexts, and the counter-evidence on aggregate demand is strong.
contestedNote: The supporting evidence is a single investor observation of forerunner teams, while independent labour-market datasets show engineering demand growing. These are not necessarily incompatible — smaller teams inside more teams would produce both — but nothing currently distinguishes that reading from the simpler one, that the shrinkage is not general.
whatWouldChangeThis: Independent survey data from outside the investor and consultancy circuit reports median team size falling
Median team size holds steady through 2027 while delivery volume rises, indicating the change is in output rather than in team shape

developmentPaths.title: Fewer, broader roles
developmentPaths.description: Small teams of generalists with machine support replace larger teams of specialists.

developmentPaths.title: Same teams, more output
developmentPaths.description: Team size holds and the gain shows up as throughput rather than as headcount reduction.

developmentPaths.title: A forerunner pattern only
developmentPaths.description: Very small teams remain characteristic of well-resourced startups and do not generalise.
